segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين. قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون. Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement.

May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Respected members of the congregation, our Prophet Muhammad warns us in numerous hadiths about the transience of this dunya (this world), about its deceptiveness, about its sweetness.

He warns us that this dunya is transient, that this dunya is, let's say, nothing. One of the most striking hadiths on this topic is the hadith narrated by Anas ibn Malik, in which the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says at the beginning of the hadith: "Yatba'ul-mayyita thalathun" – three things follow the deceased (mayyit).

What are these three things? He says: he is followed by his family, his wealth, and his, and his deeds. We will analyse this first sentence, where the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: three things follow the mayyit, or the dead person.

See how precisely the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, expresses himself at the beginning of the hadith. You know, dear brothers, when a person passes away… And in this hadith, at the beginning, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, could easily have said: the man is followed, the human being is followed, Yusuf is followed, Ibrahim is followed, and so on.
But he said: the mayyit is followed. You know, when a person passes away, people don't say: "Let's turn Dad over, let's turn Uncle over, let's turn Mother over, let's turn the son over."
Rather, people say: "Let's turn over," they say, "this mayyit." When they carry him out, they say: "Let's carry out this mayyit"; they don't say: "Let's carry out Mother, Dad," and so on.
When he is lowered into the grave, the son also doesn't say: "Let's lower Dad" – but "let's lower the mayyit".

"Let's lower the mayyit." And a person will undoubtedly, undoubtedly meet death. Here is such a striking hadith, dear brothers. Wallahi (by Allah), every sensible person should now reflect deeply on this hadith, should reflect on this hadith.

So he, that is the mayyit, is followed by three things. They follow him, he says, to the grave: his family, his wealth and his deeds. How the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, ordered them: family, wealth and deeds.
Why family? Because in this dunya the family always stands by its loved one, protecting him from this, from that, and so on.

But however much a person loves someone, and however much a mother or a father loves their child, they will not lie down with him in the grave. There is no one to protect him, there is no family to protect us when they lower us into the grave.
Also, how many times does it happen that a person buys his way out with his wealth, or pays for something he did in this dunya, in order to redeem himself or his mistake?

When a person is lowered into the grave, he will not be able, dear brothers, to redeem himself. There is no ransom. It's over, everything ends there. He will not be able to bribe anyone so that the angels don't come to question him.

He will not be able to help himself with his wealth. So, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says, his wealth and his family will, he says, go back; they cannot help him. What will remain with the person? He says, he says, his deeds will remain, whether bad or good deeds.

So, he says, those good deeds – this is mentioned in longer narrations – will come as, he says, a man with a radiant face, who will protect him in the grave from the darkness, while his bad deeds, he says, will be like darkness, for whoever has bad deeds.

That is why, dear brothers, a person must never say: "I do, I did this and that, I did this and that, and no one knows about it." He knows about it, He who created the heavens and the Earth knows about it. That is why we do everything.

He says: "I did this and that, no one knows about it. I helped so-and-so, no one knows about it." But Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: "Man 'amila salihan fa li nafsihi." He says: whoever does good deeds does them for his own sake.

For his own sake. Did you give charity? You gave it for your own sake. You did not give it for the sake of this one, or that one, or anyone else, but for your own sake. In order to make your stay in the grave easier for yourself, and also the questioning tomorrow in the Hereafter.

If you help someone, you have helped him for your own sake. If you come to the mosque and fall down in prostration to Allah – Allah is not, Allah is not in need of our prostration, nor of our prayer. The Creator of the heavens and the Earth is not in need of you and me worshipping Him.

You and I are the ones in need. We are in need of worshipping Him, because in His hands are the treasuries of the heavens and the Earth. And, as I said, a person must never say: "I did it, and no one knows about it."

He knows about it, He who created the heavens and the Earth; all of it is recorded, all of it is neatly written down there in the ledger. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the verse… And He says: whoever does bad deeds does them against himself.
Does them against himself. You do evil against yourself. We do evil against ourselves. That is why, dear brothers, you see how Islam teaches us and encourages us to do as many good deeds as possible.
This is not saying that a person should not have wealth. He should have wealth, because the strong believer, strong in faith and materially, is more beloved to Allah than the weak believer.

Why? Because he can do much more good than the believer who is not materially strong. But it also indicates that a person should not become attached to the dunya, to wealth. Ours is only what we give away in charity, and what remains behind us, someone else will take – Allah knows who.

That is why it is important that a person does good deeds, that he does them for the sake of Allah, but that he knows he is doing them for his own sake. And that is exactly, exactly what this hadith points us to.

I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who will do good deeds and will not expect people to praise them for it, [unclear], so that it is for the sake of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. I ask Him, the Exalted,

to forgive us our sins and the sins of our parents. I ask Him, the Exalted, to admit us into Jannah (Paradise). Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin. Barakallahu li wa lakum fil-Qur'anil-'azim, wa nafa'ani wa iyyakum bima fihi minal-ayati wadh-dhikril-hakim. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu,
إنه هو الغفور الرحيم.
